title: Protocol to Analyze the Bacterial Pangenome Using PAN2HGENE Software
author: de Sá, Castro Alves, et al.
materials: The following are the steps to install the external software that are part of the PAN2HGENE pipeline.3.SPAdes Installation. SPAdes is available at http://cab.spbu.ru/software/spades/, the installation process follows below.Box 3wgethttp://cab.spbu.ru/files/release3.15.3/SPAdes-3.15.3-Linux.tar.gztar -xzf SPAdes-3.15.3-Linux.tar.gza.At the end of the installation, the user must move the SPAdes folder to the /opt directory.Box 4mv SPAdes-3.15.3-Linux/ SPAdes/sudo mv SPAdes/ /opt/cd /opt/sudo chmod 777 -R SPAdes/b.To validate the installation, run the command (see Box 5), shown in Figure 1.Box 5/opt/SPAdes/bin/spades.pyFigure 1SPAdes test: Demonstrates the SPAdes test run4.PGAP Installation. The PGAP software is available at https://sourceforge.net/projects/pgap/, after downloading it follow the steps below, it is important to note that at the time of building this protocol the most current version was PGAP-1.2.1.Box 6tar -xzf PGAP-1.2.1.tar.gzmv PGAP-1.2.1/ PGAP/sudo mv PGAP/ /opt/cd /opt/sudo chmod 777 -R PGAP/a.The following step is the configuration of the PGAP script (/opt/PGAP/PGAP.pl), it can be done using gedit or other text editor preferred by the user.Box 7sudo gedit /opt/PGAP/PGAP.plb.Modify the path of the software leaving the lines of the file the same as the lines without comments (lines that do not start with the # character). It is necessary to adjust the execution path of the programs e.g., /usr/bin/formatdb according to the path where the software is in your operating system. In Box 8 below, the lines that do not start with the character # demonstrate the configuration performed in the Ubuntu operating system.Box 8### programs from BLASTmy $formatdb="/usr/bin/formatdb";my $blastall="/usr/bin/blastall";### programs from mclmy $mcl="/usr/bin/mcl";### programs from mafftmy $mafft="/usr/bin/mafft";### programs from PHYLIPmy $seqboot="/usr/lib/phylip/bin/seqboot";my $neighbor="/usr/lib/phylip/bin/neighbor";my $consense="/usr/lib/phylip/bin/consense";my $dnaml="/usr/lib/phylip/bin/dnaml";my $dnadist="/usr/lib/phylip/bin/dnadist";my $dnapars="/usr/lib/phylip/bin/dnapars";c.Look for the 3 lines below and replace "./" with "/opt/PGAP/". After the replacement the lines should look like Box 10.Box 9system("perl ./multiparanoid.pl -species ".join(".pep+",@species).".pep -unique 1");system("perl ./Blast_Filter.pl All.blastp All.pep $coverage $identity $score | $mcl - --abc -I 2.0 -o All.cluster");system("perl ./inparanoid.pl $blastall $thread $formatdb $score $global $local$species[$i].pep $species[$j].pep");Box 10system("perl /opt/PGAP/multiparanoid.pl -species ".join(".pep+",@species).".pep -unique 1");system("perl /opt/PGAP/Blast_Filter.pl All.blastp All.pep $coverage $identity $score | $mcl - --abc -I 2.0 -o All.cluster");system("perl /opt/PGAP/inparanoid.pl $blastall $thread $formatdb $score $global $local $species[$i].pep $species[$j].pep");d.Save the file and close gedit. To validate that PGAP was installed correctly, run the command below and result should be similar to this (Figure 2).Box 11/opt/PGAP/PGAP.plFigure 2PGAP test: Demonstrates the PGAP test run5.Prokka Installation. The Prokka software is available https://github.com/tseemann/prokka, to install the version for Ubuntu/Debian/Mint run the commands below.Box 12sudo apt-get install libdatetime-perl libxml-simple-perl libdigest-md5-perl git default-jre bioperlsudo cpan Bio::Perlsudo git clonehttps://github.com/tseemann/prokka.git/opt/prokkasudo chmod 777 -R /opt/prokka/opt/prokka/bin/prokka --setupdbsudo chmod 777 -R /opt/prokkaa.To verify that Prokka was installed correctly, run the command below and the result should be similar to this (Figure 3).Box 13/opt/prokka/bin/prokkaFigure 3Prokka test: Demonstrates the Prokka test run6.R Installation. The R software is installed by following the commands below.Box 14sudo apt-get updatesudo apt-get install r-base r-base-deva.After installation, run R and install the libraries.Box 15sudo Rinstall.packages('ape')install.packages("plotrix")install.packages("minpack.lm")install.packages('ctv')library('ctv')install.views('Phylogenetics')update.views('Phylogenetics')q()7.Tbl2asn Installation. The tbl2asn tool is installed by running the following commands.Box 16wget -Nftp://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/toolbox/ncbi_tools/converters/by_program/tbl2asn/linux64.tbl2asn.gzgunzip linux64.tbl2asn.gzsudo chmod +x linux64.tbl2asnmv linux64.tbl2asn /usr/local/bin/tbl2asna.And to test if everything is correct, run the command below and the result should be similar to this (Figure 4).Box 17tbl2asn --helpFigure 4Tbl2asn test: Demonstrates the Tbl2asn test run8.MySQL Installation. To install MySQL server run the following commands.Box 18sudo apt-get install mysql-serversudo mysql_secure_installationa.MySQL will ask you to create a password for the root user. Enter the password and answer Y when asked.b.The component checks to see if the new password is strong enough. Choose one of the three levels of password validation:i.Low. A password containing at least 8 characters.ii.Medium. A password containing at least 8 characters, including numeric, mixed case characters, and special characters.iii.Strong. A password containing at least 8 characters, including numeric, mixed case characters, and special characters, and compares the password to a dictionary file. Enter 0, 1, or 2 depending on the password strength you want to set.c.The script then prompts for the following security features: Remove anonymous users? Disallow root login remotely? Remove the test database and access to it? Reload privilege tables now?d.To check if your MySQL was installed correctly run the command below and the result should be similar to this (Figure 5).Box 19sudo systemctl status mysqlFigure 5MySQL test: Demonstrates the MySQL test run

steps.title: Install system dependencies
steps.instruction: Update the Ubuntu system and install all required packages, Perl modules and utilities needed by PAN2HGENE.

substeps.instruction: If any command fails, run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get upgrade, then retry the commands below.

steps.title: Install external pipeline software
steps.instruction: Download, extract, move, configure, and test each external program required by PAN2HGENE (SPAdes, PGAP, Prokka, R, tbl2asn, MySQL).

substeps.instruction: Modify the path lines (non‑commented) to match your system, e.g.:
Replace occurrences of "./" with "/opt/PGAP/" in the three system() calls (see Box 9 → Box 10).
sudo apt-get install libdatetime-perl libxml-simple-perl libdigest-md5-perl git default-jre bioperl
Test installation: tbl2asn --help (should display help message)
- Answer Y to remove anonymous users, disallow remote root login, remove test database, reload privilege tables
Test installation: sudo systemctl status mysql (service should be active)

steps.title: Download and run PAN2HGENE
steps.instruction: Obtain the PAN2HGENE jar and library, set permissions, and execute the three analysis modes (Product Identification, Comparative, Full pipeline) via the graphical interface.

substeps.instruction: Place the genome FASTA file and its paired FASTQ reads in the same folder.
1. If first use, click **Create DB**, enter root user and password.
2. Otherwise, enter root user and password and click **Connect**.
3. Click **Next**, then enter project name (e.g., "Test1") and select **Product Identification**, click **New**.
4. In the Data Input window, press **Browse** to select the FASTA file (reads must be in same folder).
5. Select the appropriate FASTQ files, specify read type and pairing orientation, then press **Add Read** (confirmation warning appears).
6. Repeat for additional genomes if needed, then click **Next**.
7. In the Parameters window, keep default values for Bowtie, Comparative Analysis, and Annotation; click **Save Data**, then **Next**.
8. Click **Perform analysis**. Monitor progress in the Logs field; when "Complete Analysis" appears, close PAN2HGENE.
Result files (located in the analysis folder):
Place all FASTA genomes (complete or draft) to be compared in one folder.
Repeat steps 1‑8 above, but in step 3 select **Comparative Analysis** instead of Product Identification.
After data input, the FASTA files will be listed (Figure 14).
When analysis finishes, results are stored in the **pgfiles** directory; files start with numbers 1‑5 and include PNG graphics (Figure 15).
Repeat the Product Identification workflow, but in step 3 select **Full Pipeline** (performs Product Identification followed automatically by Comparative Analysis).
The comparative analysis automatically generates graphics:
- Pangenome plot with Heap’s Law and pie chart of unique vs shared genes (Figure 17).
- Unique‑genes per organism plot and phylogenetic tree (Figure 18).

steps.title: Optional PATRIC annotation setup
steps.instruction: Install the PATRIC command‑line client, configure its login script, and select PATRIC as the annotation engine inside PAN2HGENE.

substeps.instruction: cp -r usr/share/patric-cli/deployment/pl /opt/patric-cli/   # copy provided p3-login.pl into the PATRIC installation directory
When configuring an analysis in the PAN2HGENE GUI, click the **PATRIC** button in the Parameters window (Figures 19‑20).
Enter your PATRIC credentials, taxonomy ID (e.g., 562 for Escherichia coli), and Domain (Bacteria), then save parameters.
